text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Conjunctivitis (Ophthalmia Neonatorum). The mother's history of gonorrhea, despite treatment four years ago, combined with the newborn's age and generalized rash, suggests potential dissemination. However, the most critical and common presentation for this organism in this age group is eye infection. I need to confirm if there are any eye discharge, swelling, or redness, and I will also request a Gram stain and culture of any ocular secretions.
